proposed_values.name: Nissan Motor Co., Ltd. (Brain-to-Vehicle programme)
proposed_values.funding_note: Corporate R&D programme inside an automaker; company-level funding, valuation and headcount are not applicable and are left null so they do not enter funding totals.
proposed_values.security_notes: Automotive EEG research programme, not a product. Nissan announced Brain-to-Vehicle (B2V) on 2018-01-03 and demonstrated elements of it on a driving simulator at CES 2018. The driver-worn EEG headset was developed with Bitbrain (Zaragoza, Spain): dry sensors, wireless, Bluetooth link to the vehicle's onboard systems per Bitbrain's 2025 article. Channel count, sampling rate, Bluetooth version, pairing and encryption are not stated by Nissan or Bitbrain. No published security documentation located. No production or on-road deployment announcement located. Verified 2026-10-06 via Nissan Global Newsroom, Nissan technology library, Bitbrain.

devices.name: Brain-to-Vehicle (B2V) EEG headset (research prototype, with Bitbrain)
devices.note: Research prototype. Signals named by Nissan: movement-related cortical potentials (MRCP, preceding intentional movement) and error-related potentials (ErrP). Nissan states systems can act '0.2 to 0.5 seconds faster than the driver'; Bitbrain's article states intent prediction 'between 0.2 and 0.8 seconds before an action' and 'up to one second' ahead after per-driver calibration. No decoding accuracy is given in either company source. Public demonstration was on a driving simulator (CES 2018). Peer-reviewed EPFL-Nissan studies report: ErrP classification accuracy 0.698 +/- 0.065 in a car simulator (N=22) and 0.682 +/- 0.059 in a real car (N=8) (Zhang et al. 2015, doi:10.1088/1741-2560/12/6/066028); anticipatory-potential decoding AUC 0.83 +/- 0.13 (braking) and 0.79 +/- 0.12 (accelerating) in a simulator (N=18), detectable 320 +/- 200 ms before action (Khaliliardali et al. 2015, doi:10.1088/1741-2560/12/6/066006). The abstracts do not name the EEG hardware used and do not use the B2V name. Headset: dry sensors, under two minutes to fit, up to eight hours of operation, Bluetooth (Bitbrain). Channel count not stated.

items.rationale: Automotive EEG programme named in the task; absent from the baseline.
items.verification_note: Nissan describes B2V as 'the world's first system of its kind'; that is the company's claim and is not adopted here.
unverified_fields: channels (not stated by Nissan or Bitbrain)
which Bitbrain model, if any, corresponds to the B2V headset (article links Hero and Diadem product pages but names neither as the B2V device)
programme status after 2020 (latest Nissan B2V-specific release located is dated 2020-07-08; the technology library page is live but undated)
company_category value (no automotive value exists in the baseline vocabulary)
first_human is the first public demonstration (CES, January 2018), not first laboratory use

proposed_values.name: Bitbrain
proposed_values.security_notes: Research EEG vendor (dry 'Minimal EEG' family: Diadem, Air, Hero; water-based Versatile EEG). Developed the driver-worn EEG headset for Nissan's Brain-to-Vehicle programme. Devices stream over Bluetooth 2.1 + EDR with microSD backup; raw data via SennsLite, LSL and a C SDK. Certification listed: CE (Directive 2014/53); no 510(k) found under applicant 'Bitbrain' in openFDA. No product security documentation located; a 2018 company blog post describes a BLE man-in-the-middle demonstration against an unnamed consumer EEG headset. Verified 2026-10-06 via bitbrain.com.
